tickets.subject: custom domain
tickets.reason: Customer wants how-to instructions for connecting a custom domain and whether free plan supports it.

draft.reply:
Hi Nina, thanks for reaching out! Custom domains are available on our Pro and Team plans, so you'll need to upgrade from Free first. Once you're on Pro or Team, here's how to connect your domain:

1. Go to Settings > Domains > Add domain, and enter your domain (like www.example.com).
2. At your registrar's DNS settings, add the record Buildbox shows you. For a subdomain like www, that's a CNAME record pointing to edge.bbx.example. For a root domain, it's an A record pointing to 192.0.2.10.
3. Wait for the status to show Verified. DNS changes can take up to an hour to show up.

After it's verified, Buildbox automatically sets up HTTPS, which usually takes up to 30 minutes. Your browser might show a "not secure" warning during that short window, which is normal.

Let us know if you run into any trouble along the way!

Buildbox Support
draft.note_for_agent: Customer is on Free plan and needs to upgrade to Pro or Team before custom domains work; reply explains this along with the DNS setup steps from KB-06.

tickets.subject: Will Buildbox overwrite my GitHub edits?
tickets.reason: The customer is asking how GitHub sync handles conflicts between manual edits and AI generated changes, which is a documented behavior question.

draft.reply:
Good news, your fix is safe. GitHub sync is two-way on the main branch, so the commit you pushed yesterday gets pulled into Buildbox within about a minute, if it hasn't already. Once it's in, any new AI generation you ask for builds on top of that code, including your fix.

The only time Buildbox holds back is if you edit the exact same file in Buildbox and on GitHub at the same moment. In that case it won't overwrite your GitHub commit, it just pauses syncing and marks the project as a conflict so you can choose which version to keep.

So as long as your fix was committed before you send the next prompt, you're good to go.

Buildbox Support
draft.note_for_agent: Straightforward KB-07 question, no account data needed, no action required.

tickets.subject: Where do I put my Stripe key
tickets.reason: Customer is asking how to properly configure a Stripe secret key, which is a documented environment variables usage question.

draft.reply:
Great question, and please don't paste your Stripe secret key into the prompt box. Prompts aren't the right place for private keys.

Instead, go to Settings > Environment and add your Stripe secret key there as a Production variable (use Stripe's test key in Preview). These values are encrypted and hidden after saving, and team members can't read them back later.

The AI can see the variable's name but never its actual value, so you can just ask it to "read the Stripe key from the environment variable STRIPE_SECRET_KEY" and it will wire things up correctly without the key itself ever being exposed.

One more thing: after adding or changing an environment variable, you'll need to deploy again for it to take effect on your live site.

Buildbox Support
draft.note_for_agent: Standard question fully covered by KB-08; no account-specific action needed.

tickets.subject: adding a teammate
tickets.reason: The customer is asking how team seat pricing and permission roles work, which is documented product information.

draft.reply:
Adding a 6th person to your Team workspace costs an extra $10 per month for that seat. This gets added to your next invoice, prorated for the rest of the current month.

To add them, go to Settings > Members > Invite and enter their email. The invite link stays valid for 7 days.

As for permissions, only the workspace Owner can delete the workspace. If you invite your contractor as an Admin or Member (not Owner), they will not be able to delete it. Admins can manage members and settings, while Members can build and deploy but not touch billing or deletion, so Member is likely the safer role for a contractor.

Let us know if you need help with anything else!

tickets.subject: Pro vs Team
tickets.reason: The customer is asking about documented differences between Pro and Team plans to decide which to use.

draft.reply:
Great question. The main difference between Pro and Team is seats. A Pro account has one seat, so only one person can log in to that account. Team comes with 5 seats included, so you and your cofounder could each have your own login within the same workspace.

Outside of that, Pro and Team give you the same things: unlimited projects, custom domains, and GitHub sync. Team just costs more ($50 vs $20 a month) and gives you a shared pool of 2,000 monthly credits instead of 500, plus slightly faster email support.

If you both need your own login and access, Team is the way to go. If one of you is fine sharing a single login, Pro would work and save you money.

2) Credit packs are different. The 200 credits you buy in a pack never expire, and they are only used after your monthly credits run out. So if you have leftover monthly credits, the pack sits untouched until those are used up.

tickets.subject: Blank preview in Safari
tickets.reason: The preview crashes in Safari with an unhandled WebGPU API error even after standard troubleshooting, indicating a compatibility bug that needs engineering investigation.

escalation.title: Blank preview in Safari 19 due to unguarded navigator.gpu.requestAdapter call
escalation.customer_impact: Single customer (lucy.grant@example.com) cannot use the preview pane in Safari 19 on Mac; app works in Chrome so a workaround exists.
evidence: The preview pane is a blank white screen in Safari 19 on my Mac. Works fine in Chrome.
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'navigator.gpu.requestAdapter')
escalation.why_not_tier_1_or_2: KB-01 only covers generic blank-preview steps (hard refresh, private window), which the customer already did; the root cause here is generated app code calling a WebGPU API without feature detection, which is a codegen behavior question that needs engineering input, not a documented user fix.
escalation.suspected_area: AI code generation producing code that calls navigator.gpu.requestAdapter without checking for WebGPU support/availability, causing an uncaught TypeError that blanks the preview in browsers/versions where WebGPU is unavailable or unflagged (e.g. this Safari 19 build).
questions_for_engineering: Can we pull the generated source for this project to confirm where navigator.gpu.requestAdapter is called and whether there is any feature detection or try/catch around it?
Should the code generator add a WebGPU availability check (e.g. if (navigator.gpu)) by default whenever it emits WebGPU calls, given inconsistent support across Safari versions?
Is this limited to Safari 19, or do we need a broader compatibility shim/fallback path in the preview runtime for browsers lacking WebGPU?
escalation.holding_reply_to_customer: Hi Lucy, thanks for the detailed report. The error points to your app calling a graphics feature (WebGPU) that isn't available in your version of Safari, which crashes the preview before it can render. This looks like a gap in how that feature was generated rather than a Safari setting on your end. We're passing this to engineering to check the generated code and add a proper fallback. In the meantime Chrome will keep working fine for you. Signed, Buildbox Support

digest.headline: Billing and credit confusion drove the most tickets this week, but a production database wipe and a GitHub sync that deleted a customer's files are the most urgent risks to fix.

themes.theme: Billing and credit charges confuse customers (wrong amounts, double charges, refund status, resets)
themes.quote: I thought I was paying $20 for Pro. Why is it $50?
themes.proposed_product_action: Ship a single billing page showing current plan price, any proration math in plain language, credit balance, and exact reset/renewal date, so customers can answer these questions themselves instead of emailing support.

themes.theme: Deploys and environment variables fail in ways customers can't fix
themes.quote: I have a launch tomorrow morning.
themes.proposed_product_action: Raise the build time limit (or make it configurable) for image-heavy builds, fix Production-scoped environment variables so they actually reach the live build, and add a stuck-deploy timeout alert.

themes.theme: Custom domain and SSL setup feels broken or scary
themes.proposed_product_action: Replace the immediate 'Not Secure' state with a clear 'Certificate provisioning, usually done in X minutes' status, and auto-page engineering if issuance exceeds 30 minutes.

themes.theme: Generation and preview bugs waste credits and break the editor
themes.quote: I lost about 30 credits for nothing.
themes.proposed_product_action: Stop deducting credits on any generation that returns a 500 error or fails, and add a feature-detection fallback so previews don't blank-screen on browsers without WebGPU support.

themes.theme: Team and account ownership changes have no clear self-serve path
themes.quote: nobody can log in as them.
themes.proposed_product_action: Let a verified Admin claim Owner role when the original owner is unreachable, and support self-serve login/billing email changes without disrupting the active plan.

themes.theme: Pricing tiers and compliance needs block growth and nonprofit customers
themes.quote: $50 a month is a lot for us.
themes.proposed_product_action: Publish a nonprofit/education discount and a self-serve NDA-gated SOC 2 report request on the pricing page, and clarify Pro vs Team seat limits so small teams don't have to ask support.

themes.theme: GitHub sync overwrites or deletes customer code without warning
themes.quote: I did not ask for that, my prompt was to change a button color.
themes.proposed_product_action: Require a diff preview and explicit confirmation before the AI pushes commits to main, and scope AI edits so unrelated files/folders can't be deleted by a single prompt.

themes.theme: Data loss and export fears around production databases
themes.proposed_product_action: Add automatic point-in-time backups of the production database taken before every redeploy, with a one-click restore, and make a full code+data export a standard self-serve action.
